turn.user_message: a hospital is too dynamic. will such hard rules actually be possible to implement? there will be a lot of resistance
turn.context: Two objections, two treatments. Resistance is conceded and parked for part 3. Too dynamic is tested against the hospital’s own figures.

transcript.label: Transcript turn 23 · “A hospital is too dynamic. Will such hard rules work?”

text: Resistance is real, and it is most of part 3. But too dynamic is worth testing first, because your numbers point the other way.
bullets: 89% full, a 6.5 day stay, about 41 admissions a day. The total is steady, even though no single bed is.
What is unknown is which bed frees when. What is known is how many will free, and roughly when. The mapping only uses that.
What is fixed is when a decision is made, not what is decided. When something moves, the plan re-runs and only the affected times change.
chat.pointer: Follow the routes through the maze. Then try a change and watch the plan re-run.
chat.invite: Resistance deserves more than a line. Shall I take you into part 3?
chat.note: Fix when decisions are made, not what is decided.
prompts: Tell me more about why a Discharge Manager is needed
What if a doctor will not give a date?

blocks.title: Fixed times, free decisions
blocks.deck: Three routes were tried. Only one keeps both the plan and the doctor’s call.

blocks.start: A day that feels too dynamic
blocks.goal: A plan that holds on a busy day

routes.name: Fix what gets decided
routes.why: Who is fit to leave stays a clinical call. A rule on that would be broken every day.

routes.name: No fixed times at all
routes.why: Then nothing is ready the evening before. Every afternoon gets rebuilt, as it is today.

routes.name: Fix when decisions are made
routes.why: The 2 PM mapping, the 5 PM check and the 6 PM freeze. What gets decided stays with the doctor.

sheets.title: Fix what gets decided
sheets.text: A rule on who goes home would sit on top of a clinical call. Doctors would break it daily, and they would be right to.

sheets.title: No fixed times at all
sheets.text: Without fixed times, nobody can plan the evening before. That is how the day runs now: rebuilt every afternoon.

lines.label: Why it fails
lines.value: Nothing is ready the evening before

sheets.title: Fix when decisions are made
sheets.text: The times are fixed. The decisions are not. A step-down that slips is an input to the next pass, not a breach.

lines.label: Fixed
lines.value: When the 2 PM, 5 PM and 6 PM decisions happen

lines.label: Left alone
lines.value: Who is fit to leave, emergencies, a step-down that slips

sheets.entry: Which decision moves most often at your hospital?

tries.title: A patient stays one more night

loop.title: The plan re-runs
loop.line: Only for the beds it touches

loop.title: The change is recorded
loop.line: A logged event, not a rule broken

sheets.title: An emergency arrives
sheets.text: Emergencies arrive when they arrive. A bed is held back for them. The plan re-runs for the beds that move, and nothing else changes.
sheets.entry: How many emergencies do you admit on a usual day?

sheets.title: A step-down slips a day
sheets.text: The ICU patient stays another day. The next pass takes that in. The patient waiting for that bed gets a new call-in time.

lines.label: What moves
lines.value: The bed it was meant to free

sheets.entry: How often does a step-down slip?

sheets.title: A patient stays one more night
sheets.text: The doctor decides the patient is not fit to leave. That is the doctor’s call. The plan follows it and records the change.
sheets.entry: Who would tell the desk at your hospital?
